# AmRent

**What this is:** the resident screening service — background, credit, criminal, bankruptcy and eviction history — reached only from inside Rent Manager.

**Status:** current — 2026-08-30

## The facts
- **What they supply:** applicant screening reports covering identity, SSN/ITIN, **credit history, criminal background, bankruptcy and eviction history**.
- **Who uses it:** the **Screening Coordinator** runs the screening; the Community Manager and Sales own intake and the application file; Directors decide escalated cases. Process owner is the Director of Sales & Marketing and the Director of Operations jointly (SOP 006).
- **The access rule: screening runs through AmRent inside Rent Manager — never outside either system** (SOP 006). There is no direct-login path in any SOP; the integration is the only documented route.
- **The results clock: up to 72 hours, and no preliminary decision or outcome may be communicated to the prospect before full results are received.**
- **The income standard applied alongside it: gross monthly income must be at least 2.5x the monthly lot rent.** Below that is a basis for denial; the calculation is documented in Rent Manager. R:I and D:I ratios are both calculated.
- Required file before screening: government-issued photo ID, income documentation, signed consent form, all fields complete, application fee paid. The older PDF is stricter — **two recent paystubs, W-2s, and two to three months of bank statements, all pages.**
- **The denial confidentiality rule: do not send a denial notice to the prospect before notifying the Community Manager.** Denial notices must comply with fair housing and adverse-action notice requirements — the recording schedule adds "same screen, every applicant."
- Escalated reviews carry **a limited summary only** — never the full application packet.
- **How critical: high.** Every new resident in the portfolio is screened here, and there is no second screening vendor named anywhere in 242 process files. Lose AmRent and move-ins stop: no screening means no approval, and no approval means SOP 103 cannot proceed — its own gate is "no move-in is approved without all required documents and a signed lease on file."
- The dependency is doubled by the access route: because AmRent is reached only through Rent Manager, a Rent Manager outage takes screening with it, and an AmRent outage leaves the Rent Manager "Run Screening" step dead with no documented workaround.
- **Known problems:** the vendor's name is spelled three ways within and across documents — **AmRent / Amrent / AMRENT**. Two generations of SOP 006 disagree on **who has final approval authority on an escalated applicant** — the current draft says the Directors of Sales and Operations decide jointly; the older PDF says "Regional Manager has final approval authority." The two also handle a denial differently: one ends at status Denied, the other moves the prospect to Lost, which changes reporting.
- The tracker records that SOP 006 "absorbs the two separate AMRENT/Prospect Screening tracker rows" — **the merge happened on the tracker, not in the documents**, so there is still no standalone screening SOP.
- The PDF names a Screening Coordinator, **Keiter Abreu**, and a District Manager, **Jhoiner Perez**, who appear nowhere else in the process library.

## Decisions
- None recorded yet. Final approval authority on an escalated applicant — Directors jointly or Regional Manager — is unresolved.
